scholarships.title: Sonja Davies Peace Award Fund
scholarships.official_source: New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura

existing.description: The Sonja Davies Peace Award Fund promotes initiatives that advance peace in New Zealand and is open to a woman, or a group led by a woman, developing an initiative at home, school, the workplace or in the community. It commemorates Sonja Davies, a New Zealand women's rights campaigner and politician, and includes work on family violence, inter-group understanding, mediation and conflict resolution. Awards are worth up to NZD 4,000, and the Trust publishes the 2026 application window as 12 to 30 October.
eligibility: Be a woman, or be the project leader of a group where the leader is a woman
Be one of: an informal group with peace promotion among its stated aims, an individual enrolled at a tertiary institution, or a formal group
Be a New Zealand citizen, or hold a resident class visa, and currently live in New Zealand
Not have previously received a New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura Award
Be developing an initiative that will advance peace in New Zealand
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to a woman, or a group whose project leader is a woman, who is developing an initiative to advance peace in New Zealand. The three stated eligible categories are an informal group with peace promotion among its aims, an individual enrolled at a tertiary institution, and a formal group. Applicants must be a New Zealand citizen or hold a resident class visa and currently live in New Zealand, and must not have previously received a New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura award.
benefits: Up to NZD 4,000 of project funding
Recognition as a Sonja Davies Peace Award recipient from a national women's charitable trust
Support for initiatives addressing family violence, inter-group understanding, mediation and conflict resolution
coverage: Grant of up to NZD 4,000 toward the cost of the applicant's peace initiative
requirements: Must submit a project timeline and budget indicating how the funds will be spent
Must describe the initiative and how it will advance peace in New Zealand
Must demonstrate experience of and capability to conduct the initiative
Must not have previously received a New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura Award
application_method: Apply during the published 12 to 30 October 2026 window
Submit an application that sets out experience of and demonstrated capability to conduct the initiative
Include a description of the initiative, how it will advance peace in New Zealand, and a project timeline and budget
existing.selection_notes: The Trust's selection panel considers three things: experience of and demonstrated capability to conduct the initiative; a description of the initiative and how it will advance peace in New Zealand; and a project timeline and budget indicating how funds will be spent. Previous recipients of any New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura award are ineligible, so this cannot be combined with the Trust's Education, Research or Personal Growth awards.
existing.best_fit: A woman, or a woman-led group, already working on peace, family violence, mediation or conflict resolution in New Zealand, with a costed project plan.
existing.notes: This is a project grant, not a course scholarship, though one of three applicant categories is a student enrolled at a tertiary institution. It is one of the named funds of New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura.
existing.duration: One-off grant for a defined project with a submitted timeline and budget
existing.application_period: The Trust publishes that the application window is open from 12 to 30 October 2026. That window opens eight days after this verification date.
existing.program_type: Charitable trust project grant (women-led peace and conflict-resolution initiatives, open to tertiary students)

scholarships.title: Toloa Tertiary Scholarship (Toloa Scholarships - tertiary stream, Ministry for Pacific Peoples)
scholarships.degree: Tertiary (second year and beyond of a full-time STEM degree)
scholarships.official_source: Ministry for Pacific Peoples, New Zealand Government

existing.description: The Toloa Tertiary Scholarship supports Pacific students in New Zealand who are in the second year or beyond of a full-time STEM degree. The Ministry for Pacific Peoples funds it and Le Va administers applications, disbursement and reporting, and up to NZD 10,000 for one year of full-time study is paid directly to the institution. Applications for the 2026 round closed at 5pm on 9 February 2026, and students in their final year or Year 3 of STEM study are excluded because they can access the Government fees-free programme.
eligibility: Have completed at least one year of study
Be entering their second year of study or beyond
Not be in a final year or in Year 3 of STEM studies, because those students can access the Government fees-free programme and are therefore not eligible for Toloa Scholarships
existing.eligibility_summary: Pacific students who have completed at least one year of study and are continuing full-time STEM study in New Zealand, entering their second year or beyond.
benefits: Tertiary students entering their second year of STEM study can receive up to $10,000 for one year of full-time study
Funds are paid directly to the tertiary institution and can be accessed through the institution's Scholarships Office or equivalent
coverage: Up to NZD 10,000 for one year of full-time study, paid directly to the tertiary institution
requirements: Be continuing full-time STEM study and not be in the final year or Year 3 of a STEM programme
Apply through Le Va, which administers the application process, disbursement of funds and reporting
documents: Full eligibility criteria and guidance from Le Va
application_method: Visit the Le Va Toloa Scholarships page for full eligibility criteria, guidance and the application form
Contact the Le Va team at Toloa@leva.co.nz with questions
existing.selection_notes: The Ministry funds the scholarships and Le Va administers them, managing the application process, disbursement of funds and reporting. Ten tertiary scholarships were on offer for the 2026 academic year, alongside 400 secondary scholarships.
existing.best_fit: Pacific students already in their second year or beyond of a full-time STEM degree in New Zealand who are not in their final year or Year 3.
existing.notes: Students in their final year, or in Year 3 of their STEM studies, can access the Government fees-free programme and therefore will not be eligible for Toloa Scholarships. The award is a capped contribution, not a full-cost scholarship.
existing.application_period: Applications for 2026 tertiary scholarships are closed; tertiary applications closed at 5pm on Monday 9 February 2026. The Ministry republishes the scheme annually with a new closing date each year.
existing.program_type: Government scholarship (funded by the Ministry for Pacific Peoples, administered by Le Va)
